name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, 276 KB, title "Procurement | National electronic tool", serving a live contract-notice listing distinct from the site root. The English surface is served by the operator, not a translation layer.
limitations: Supplier registration and submission routes were not separately verified and are recorded as null rather than guessed.

name: e-Vergabe — Vergabeplattform des Bundes
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 400 with title "e-Vergabe: Cookies benötigt", redirecting to ?cookieCheck. That is a cookie gate, not an absent platform, so nothing about the system's content was established by fetch. Germany additionally has no single national portal — federal, 16 Länder and municipal systems coexist — so this record covers the federal platform only.
limitations: Content behind the cookie gate is unverified; no discovery, registration or submission route is asserted.
Covers federal procurement only. Länder and municipal platforms are out of scope for Wave T1.

name: Udbud.dk
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200 but only 902 bytes with title "udbud.dk" — a client-rendered shell. Reachability was established; procurement function was not. The operating authority was not established and is recorded as null rather than assumed.
limitations: Procurement function not established by fetch; requires rendered-browser verification.

name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily
operator: Publications Office of the European Union
evidenceNote: The European Commission identifies TED as the official portal publishing the S series of the Official Journal. Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200; /en/search/search resolves to /en/advanced-search, title "Find notices easily on TED with Advanced Search". TED is a notice publication and discovery system: bidding happens on the buyer's own system, which is why electronicSubmission is "no" rather than unknown.
limitations: Publishes above-threshold notices; below-threshold opportunities live on national systems.
Whether a given foreign supplier may bid is set by each individual notice, not by TED, so no eligibility is asserted here.

name: eTenders
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, resolving to /epps/home.do with title "European Dynamics - Welcome to eTenders". The platform is operated by the Office of Government Procurement and built on European Dynamics' ePPS; the vendor is recorded separately because a software supplier is not a procurement authority. The commercial instance at irl.eu-supply.com is not published as a second platform.
limitations: The documented quick-search route returned an empty 200 body and is therefore not published as a discovery URL.

name: TenderNed
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200 but only 117 bytes and no title — a client-rendered shell. Reachability established, procurement function not. PIANOo, which the European Commission lists as the Dutch entry point, is an expertise centre rather than a tender platform and is deliberately not published as one.
limitations: Procurement function not established by fetch; requires rendered-browser verification.

name: Platforma e-Zamówienia
evidenceNote: Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, title "EZamowienia", on the marketplace-client path distinct from the site root. The European Commission's entry for Poland points at uzp.gov.pl, which redirects to a gov.pl authority page and is the regulator rather than the platform; the platform is recorded here instead.
limitations: The search surface is client-rendered, so the extent of public search without an account was not established.

name: BASE — Contratos Públicos Online
operator: Instituto dos Mercados Públicos, do Imobiliário e da Construção
evidenceNote: The European Commission lists BASE as Portugal's public procurement portal. Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, 90 KB on the English surface. BASE is principally a contracts and award transparency database rather than a bidding system, which is why no submission route is asserted.
limitations: The documented /Base4/en/pesquisa/ search route answered HTTP 404 while serving the homepage body — a soft 404 — so it is not published as a discovery URL.

name: SEAP / SICAP
evidenceNote: The European Commission lists e-licitatie.ro as Romania's electronic public procurement system. Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, title "SEAP", and the contract-notices list path resolves to a distinct live listing surface.
limitations: The operating authority is recorded from the platform's public identification and was not separately re-verified against a statutory source.

name: e-JN — Elektronsko javno naročanje
evidenceNote: The European Commission lists ejn.gov.si as Slovenia's electronic public procurement system. Fetched 2026-08-11: HTTP 200, title "Elektronsko javno naročanje e-JN".
limitations: The /eJN2 path redirects back to the site root, so it is a homepage fallback rather than a distinct discovery route and is not published as one.
